section_path: 5.3 Subjective Weights Analysis: Analytical Hierarchy Process

note: Eight measured regions over five pages of a 22-page paper, and every one is an exhibit: 3 figure rows and 5 printed tables, no exclusions and no declared gaps. The exhibit count is tiny because all but three pages are prose, equations and references. Two families: 2 `line` (the Google Trends sketches on p10, blue lines with no y scale and unkeyed peak letters) and 1 `flowchart-or-schematic` (the AHP hierarchy on p12, box-and-arrow), plus 5 `table-grid`. Every exhibit uses the colon form and flat numbering, Figure 1 to Figure 3 and Table 1 to Table 5. All five tables are pasted raster images whose captions are pixels too, so all five are typed from the crop and all five print their caption BELOW the grid, against the lane's table convention. All five share one construction - blue header band, alternating tints, thin vertical rules - so all five are `vertical-rules` with `zebra` true, and Table 5 alone prints a tight colon ('Table 5:Top 5 ...') with no space. The three weight tables repeat one AHP weight vector verbatim across the three sports. The paper's only numbered citation is wrong: p12 cites 'Figure 2' for the hierarchy that is printed there as Figure 3, so the mention sits on Figure 2 with lead_pages -2 and the hierarchy itself has none.
rules: The paper numbers its exhibits flatly - 'Figure 1:' to 'Figure 3:' and 'Table 1:' to 'Table 5:' - so the colon form of the enum fits every record [caption.numbering].

All five tables are pasted rasters: the grid, its blue header band and its caption line are pixels, so no caption text is in the text layer and every one is recorded with `caption_source: 'typed-from-crop'` [caption.verbatim].
All five table captions print BELOW their grids, against the lane's convention that tables caption above, so the position is recorded as printed rather than normalised [caption.position].

All five tables share one construction - a solid blue header band, alternating light blue body tints and thin vertical rules between the columns - so all five are `vertical-rules` with `zebra` true, and none is booktabs [table.rule_style].

The three weight tables share one AHP row verbatim across football, basketball and baseball - the same seven-entry vector - because the subjective weights are common to all sports, while the Maxent&GRC row differs in each [table.rows].

p10's two charts are Google Trends screenshots with no y axis scale, no frame and no legend; the peak letters A to G and A to N are in-figure annotations that are never keyed, so `legend` is `none` [geometry.legend].

Figure 3 is a box-and-arrow hierarchy on a raster, recorded `flowchart-or-schematic` because every node is a labelled rectangle joined by drawn edges, not an unboxed node-link drawing [geometry.family].

The paper's only numbered citation is broken: p12 says 'As is vividly shown in Figure 2' while introducing the hierarchy printed on that page as Figure 3, so the mention is recorded on Figure 2 with `lead_pages` -2 and Figure 3's block is left empty [mention.lead_pages].

The p10 sketches and the p12 hierarchy are all rasters with captions that survive in the text layer, while the p15-p17 tables are rasters whose captions do not - so `caption_source` is read per exhibit and not assumed from `kind` [caption.verbatim].

Every heading is numbered except the stray 'Model' line on p16 and the 'References' line, so `section_path` quotes the printed numbered headings and `section_numbered` is true throughout [place.section_path].

tables.note: The shortlist table, pasted in as a raster: header 'Ranking | Football | Basketball | Baseball' over five ranked rows (1 Tom Osborne / John Wooden / Cliff Gustafson down to 5 Bear Bryant / Clair Bee / Bibb Falk). A full-width dark blue header band with white bold labels, body rows tinted alternately light blue and white, faint rules between the rows, thin vertical rules between all four columns and a closed frame, so `rule_style` is `vertical-rules` and `zebra` is true. The only numeric column is the printed rank. Its caption prints BELOW the grid, which is the reverse of the lane's table rule [caption.position].
